findings.title: Advance-tax interest exposure — ss.424/425 (₹1,92,561)
findings.detail: Advance tax paid (₹8,00,000) falls short of the assessed tax (₹37,68,629) this year. At 1%/month simple interest: ₹1,18,745 under s.424 (shortfall below the 90% floor, 4 months to the non-audit (31 Jul) due date) + ₹73,816 under s.425 (quarter-by-quarter installment shortfalls). Both keep accruing past the due date until actually paid — this is the exposure AS OF the due date, not a final number.
findings.recommendation: Pay the shortfall before filing to stop s.424 interest accruing further; s.425's quarter-by-quarter amount is fixed once the year ends and doesn't grow. If the year isn't over yet, revise the remaining installment(s) upward.

findings.title: Form 10-IEA required to elect the old regime with business/professional income
findings.detail: The old tax regime is selected and business/professional (PGBP) income is on file. Unlike a salary-only filer, an assessee with PGBP income can't just choose the old regime on the ITR itself — Form 10-IEA must be filed by the s.139(1) due date, and once withdrawn from the old regime this way, old-regime eligibility is gone for good except for those without PGBP income.
findings.recommendation: File Form 10-IEA before the ITR due date. Confirm this taxpayer hasn't already exercised and withdrawn the election in a prior year, which would make the old regime unavailable regardless of what's chosen this year.

findings.title: India residency status may not match the facts on file — derived RNOR, recorded ROR
findings.detail: Re-deriving India's residential-status determination from the same raw facts Layer 1's own wizard uses (day-count, the 4-year lookback, RNOR sub-status conditions, employment/PIO-visit exceptions, s.6(1A) deemed-residency, incorporation/POEM, or control-and-management, depending on entity type) produces RNOR, but the recorded final_india_residency_status is ROR.
findings.recommendation: Re-run the Layer 1 India residency wizard, or verify the underlying residency facts were entered consistently — this looks like a wizard or data-entry error.

findings.title: $482 of lottery/gaming winnings — flat 30% (s.128/194), no exemptions
findings.detail: This income is taxed at a flat 30% with no basic exemption threshold, no Chapter VI-A deduction and no §156 rebate — it's now included in the India tax total and the FTC/double-tax figures above.
findings.recommendation: Confirm US-side treatment of the same winnings separately from the general FTC computation — a flat-rate/graduated-rate mismatch on the same income can leave a residual gap the average-rate FTC approximation misses.

findings.title: Brought-forward losses fully set off this year
findings.detail: All eligible prior-year losses were absorbed against this year's income: ₹90,000 STCG loss vs. STCG. The India tax computed above already reflects this — no residual carry-forward remains.
findings.recommendation: Confirm the set-off is reported correctly on Schedule CFL/BFLA of the ITR, matching the ordering above.

documents.name: FinCEN Form 114 (FBAR)
documents.desc: Report of Foreign Bank and Financial Accounts.
documents.why: Aggregate peak balance across all foreign (Indian) accounts exceeded USD 10,000.

documents.name: IRS Form 8938 (FATCA)
documents.desc: Statement of Specified Foreign Financial Assets, filed with Form 1040.
documents.why: Specified foreign financial assets exceeded the Form 8938 reporting threshold for your filing status/residence.

documents.name: IRS Form 1116 (Foreign Tax Credit)
documents.desc: Claims credit for income tax paid to India against US tax liability.
documents.why: Indian income tax was paid on income that is also taxable in the US.

documents.name: IRS Form 2555 (FEIE)
documents.desc: Foreign Earned Income Exclusion / foreign housing exclusion.
documents.why: FEIE was elected on foreign earned income.

documents.name: IRS Form 8833 (Treaty-Based Position)
documents.desc: Discloses a treaty-based return position (e.g. Article 4 tie-breaker).
documents.why: A DTAA tie-breaker or treaty rate is being relied upon to override default US taxation.

documents.name: IRS Form 8621 (PFIC)
documents.desc: Information return for Passive Foreign Investment Companies — one per fund.
documents.why: Holdings in Indian mutual funds / ETFs are PFICs and require annual reporting (punitive §1291 regime unless QEF/MTM elected).

documents.name: IRS Form 5471 (CFC)
documents.desc: Information return for US persons owning ≥10% of a foreign corporation.
documents.why: You own ≥10% of an Indian company — potential Subpart F / GILTI inclusion.

documents.name: IRS Form 8865
documents.desc: Return for US persons with interests in a foreign partnership.
documents.why: You hold an interest in an Indian partnership/LLP.

documents.name: IRS Form 3520 / 3520-A
documents.desc: Reporting of foreign gifts and transactions with foreign trusts.
documents.why: Foreign gift > USD 100,000 received, or you are a grantor/beneficiary of a foreign trust (note: Indian PPF/EPF may be treated as trusts).

documents.name: IRS Form 1040-NR
documents.desc: Non-resident alien income tax return.
documents.why: You are (or elect to be treated as) a US non-resident alien for this year.

documents.name: IRS Form 8960 (NIIT)
documents.desc: Net Investment Income Tax (3.8%).
documents.why: MAGI exceeded the NIIT threshold and net investment income is present.

documents.name: IRS Form 8959 (Additional Medicare Tax)
documents.desc: Additional 0.9% Medicare tax on wages/SE income above the filing-status threshold, and reconciles employer over/under-withholding.
documents.why: Additional Medicare Tax is owed and is not offset by the Foreign Tax Credit.

documents.name: California Form 540 (Resident Income Tax Return)
documents.desc: California state income tax return — computed on worldwide income for a full-year CA resident, including Indian-source income. CA grants no credit for tax paid to a foreign country.
documents.why: State-of-residence facts on file point to California, and CA taxes worldwide income independently of the federal treaty position.

documents.name: New York Form IT-201 (Resident Income Tax Return)
documents.desc: New York state income tax return — computed on worldwide income for a full-year NY resident, including Indian-source income. NY grants no credit for tax paid to a foreign country.
documents.why: State-of-residence facts on file point to New York, and NY taxes worldwide income independently of the federal treaty position.

documents.name: Form 44 (India FTC)
documents.desc: Statement of foreign income & foreign tax, filed before the ITR due date.
documents.why: Foreign (US) income is being offered to tax in India and FTC u/s 90/91 is claimed. Schedule FSI/TR must accompany the ITR.

documents.name: Tax Residency Certificate (TRC)
documents.desc: Issued by the other contracting state (IRS Form 6166 for the US).
documents.why: DTAA relief / treaty rate is being claimed — a TRC is mandatory u/s 159(8).

documents.name: Form 41
documents.desc: Self-declaration accompanying the TRC, filed electronically on the ITR portal.
documents.why: Treaty benefit claimed and the TRC does not contain all particulars required u/r 75.

documents.name: Schedule FA (Foreign Assets)
documents.desc: Disclosure of foreign assets/accounts in the Indian ITR.
documents.why: You are Resident & Ordinarily Resident (ROR) and hold US bank accounts, securities or other foreign assets.

documents.name: Schedule FSI & Schedule TR
documents.desc: Foreign Source Income and Tax Relief schedules in the ITR.
documents.why: Foreign income is offered to tax and relief u/s 90/91 is claimed.

documents.name: Form 145 / Form 146 (was 15CA / 15CB)
documents.desc: Remittance certificates for foreign outward remittances.
documents.why: Outward remittances under LRS / to non-residents were made during the year. Renumbered from Form 15CA/15CB effective 1 Apr 2026 under the Income-tax Rules, 2026 (Rule 220) — the old numbers still apply to remittances made before that date.

documents.name: Schedule AL (Assets & Liabilities)
documents.desc: Disclosure of assets and liabilities at cost, filed with the ITR.
documents.why: Total income exceeds ₹50 lakh — Schedule AL is mandatory at this threshold u/s 139(1) (ITR-2/3/5 filers).

documents.name: Form 3CB / 3CD (Tax Audit Report)
documents.desc: Chartered Accountant's tax-audit report and statement of particulars, filed before the ITR due date.
documents.why: Business turnover exceeds the s.44AB tax-audit threshold (₹1 crore, or ₹10 crore where cash receipts and payments are each ≤5% of the total).

documents.name: IRS Form 8802 (Application for US Residency Certification)
documents.desc: Application to the IRS for Form 6166 — the US residency certificate India's TRC requirement expects the other contracting state to issue.
documents.why: DTAA relief is being claimed on Indian-source income — Form 6166 must be requested via Form 8802 before it can be filed with the Indian TRC/Form 41 paperwork; IRS processing typically takes 4-6+ weeks, so file well ahead of the India due date.

documents.name: IRS Form 6251 (Alternative Minimum Tax)
documents.desc: Computes AMT and reconciles it against regular tax liability.
documents.why: AMT preference items (commonly an ISO exercise, or the SALT-cap add-back) push tentative minimum tax above the regular tax for the year.

documents.name: IRS Form 8288 / 8288-A / 8288-B (FIRPTA Withholding)
documents.desc: Withholding certificate and returns for a foreign person's disposition of US real property.
documents.why: A US real property interest was disposed of by a foreign person — 15% FIRPTA withholding applies at closing unless a Form 8288-B withholding certificate reduces it.

documents.name: Form 3CEB (Transfer Pricing Certification)
documents.desc: Chartered Accountant's report on international transactions with associated enterprises, filed before the ITR due date u/s 92E.
documents.why: A cross-border related-party ownership relationship is on file — international transactions with that entity must be reported and certified, independent of whether pricing is at arm's length.

documents.name: Form 26AS / AIS / TIS
documents.desc: Annual tax-credit statement (26AS) and the Annual/Taxpayer Information Statements — the pre-filled record every ITR should be reconciled against before filing.
documents.why: Indian income is on file for this taxpayer — TDS, advance tax and reported high-value transactions should be cross-checked against these statements before the return is filed.

documents.name: Form 16 / Form 16A (TDS Certificates)
documents.desc: Salary (Form 16) and non-salary (Form 16A) TDS certificates issued by each deductor.
documents.why: Indian income subject to TDS is on file — hold the certificate from each deductor to reconcile against Form 26AS/AIS and support the credit claimed in the ITR.

documents.name: LRS Form A2 (Outward Remittance Declaration)
documents.desc: Declaration furnished to the remitting bank for each outward remittance under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme.
documents.why: Outward remittances under LRS were made this year — each remittance requires its own Form A2 filed with the bank at the time of transfer, separate from the annual Form 145/146 (was 15CA/15CB) return-time reporting.

documents.name: IRS Form 4868 (Extension Request)
documents.desc: Automatic 6-month extension of time to file (not to pay) the US return.
documents.why: Must be filed by the original due date to legally reach the extended deadline already on your Compliance Calendar — the extension does not happen automatically.

Old regime: s.123 (cap ₹1.5L) + s.124(1B) NPS (cap ₹50k) + s.126 health insurance (cap ₹75k) + employer NPS s.124(2) (uncapped) + s.153 savings interest (cap ₹10k)
Gross total income less Chapter VI-A deductions

Progressive slab-rate tax under the OLD regime, applied to ₹1,12,02,000 of normal-rate income (salary, house property, business, other sources, after Chapter VI-A deductions and brought-forward loss set-off). Capital gains and other special-rate income are taxed separately, not at slab rates.

rows.label: Tax on special-rate income (196/197/198 gains + 115BBH VDA + 128/194 winnings)

trace.formula: s.196 STCG @ 20% + s.198 LTCG @ 12.5% (listed/STT-paid, net of the ₹1,25,000 exemption) + s.197 LTCG @ 12.5% (unlisted/foreign — no exemption, separate section, does not pool with s.198's threshold) + s.115BBH VDA/crypto @ 30% flat (no set-off, ever) + s.128/194 lottery/betting/gaming winnings @ 30% flat, no exemption (each broken out below)

Same 12.5% rate as s.198, but NO ₹1,25,000 exemption — that's textually specific to s.198's listed/STT-paid gains and doesn't pool with s.197, so this whole amount is taxable from the first rupee. Fed by: unlisted buy-back gains, foreign-equity gains (e.g. US stocks), unlisted bonds without STT, non-equity-oriented/non-specified mutual funds (debt MF acquired pre-Apr-2023, 35-65%-equity hybrid funds, international/FoF funds no longer meeting s.50AA's specified-fund test), and Chapter XII-A specified listed equity/debentures/government securities sold to a third party (s.115E's LTCG rate has no exemption either, unlike ordinary s.198) — all held >24 months, or >12 months for a listed bond, specified debenture/govt security, or specified listed equity

Virtual digital assets (crypto) are taxed at a flat 30% on positive gains only — no LTCG/STCG distinction, no holding-period threshold, no exemption or indexation, and crucially NO loss set-off is allowed at all, not even against a gain from a different VDA in the same year, and no carry-forward. Any losing VDA transaction is simply excluded, never netted against a gain
Only for a resident individual (not NR, not HUF/AOP/BOI/trust) whose normal-rate income is at or below the threshold — lesser of tax at slab rates and the statutory cap

Progressive surcharge (10%/15%/25%/37% bands by total income) on tax before cess, with marginal relief so the tax increase never exceeds the income increase over the threshold; capital-gains/dividend-type special-rate income is capped at a 15% surcharge rate
4% of (tax after rebate + surcharge)
Tax at slab rates + tax on special-rate income − §156 rebate + surcharge + cess
Ordinary income (wages + business/self-employment + interest + non-qualified dividends + STCG + rental + pension) + preferential income (LTCG + qualified dividends)
Total income less above-the-line adjustments (student-loan interest, capped at $2,500, + half of self-employment tax)
Standard deduction for filing status SINGLE — used because it exceeds (or the taxpayer elected) itemizing
AGI less deduction
Progressive federal brackets (10%-37%, filing status SINGLE) applied to $0 of ordinary taxable income (taxable income less the LTCG/QDI portion, which is taxed separately below)
0%/15%/20% long-term capital gains brackets, stacked on top of ordinary taxable income
Zero — either no net investment income, or MAGI doesn't exceed the filing-status threshold

scopeNotes.title: GAAR is not evaluated
scopeNotes.body: India's General Anti-Avoidance Rule can recharacterize arrangements that lack commercial substance — a facts-and-circumstances judgment no rules engine can safely make. WISING flags mechanical conflicts only; whether an arrangement invites GAAR scrutiny remains a professional call.

scopeNotes.title: STT is not computed as a levy
scopeNotes.body: Securities Transaction Tax charged on trades (raised on F&O by Finance Act 2026) isn't calculated here. The stt_paid flag on each transaction drives the capital-gains regime (s.196/198 vs s.197) — the levy amount itself is neither a tax credit nor a capital-gains deduction, so nothing downstream depends on it.

scopeNotes.title: Your obligations as a TDS deductor aren't tracked
scopeNotes.body: The Withholding page covers tax withheld FROM this taxpayer's income. Duties in the opposite direction — deducting TDS on payments the business makes to vendors, contractors, or professionals — aren't monitored as a compliance obligation in their own right, though the resulting s.40(a) expense disallowance for TDS failures (and s.40A(3) cash-payment / s.43B(h) MSME-overdue disallowances) does flow into business income (Phase 1).

scopeNotes.title: Clubbing amounts are taken as entered
scopeNotes.body: Spousal and minor-child clubbed income entered in Layer 1 is taxed as given. WISING doesn't trace asset transfers between family members to detect clubbing that should have been reported but wasn't.

scopeNotes.title: Document-upload extraction is simulated
scopeNotes.body: Every "upload to auto-fill" feature in Layer 1 (Form 26AS, Lower-TDS certificate, bank statements, property documents) is a demo simulation with representative values — not live OCR. Figures sourced from an upload should be treated as manually-entered until real extraction ships.

Reasons: Total income exceeds ₹50,00,000 (₹1,32,65,000); Capital gains beyond the s.198-only allowance (STCG and/or non-s.198 LTCG present); Crypto/VDA gains or sale activity on file; Lottery/betting/online-gaming winnings on file (s.128/194); Brought-forward losses on file; Speculative or F&O business income on file. Layer 1 India hasn't produced its own recommendation for this profile (itr_recommendation.form is unset) — this is WISING's own independent computation, run unconditionally, not a hedge pending the frontend.
